scope: Two fresh Google client logins in Safari after deployment of the pool-identity and one-query host-exchange fixes. Timings start at the workspace document navigation after Google; they exclude account-choice time and do not establish full workspace readiness.
findings: Live code exchange now reports two SQL queries, and each client-to-host exchange reports one.
The first contentful paint remains later than the startup response: 1.292 s and 1.670 s.

The initial web HTML has an empty root. The web entry awaits account sign-in before starting catalog boot and importing the workspace. This leaves no workspace content until the client module is loaded and mounted.
There is no measured first-paint improvement in these two observations, despite reduced query counts.
limits: Two observations are not production percentiles or a controlled before/after experiment. Safari Web Inspector was open; cache state and host machine load were not controlled.
HTML-response-end to first-contentful-paint is a measured interval, not a frame-by-frame measurement of a white screen.
Safari switched to an Expo tab during preparation for run 2; the benchmark resumed in the Solus tab before Google login.
After run 2 startup, a console timing command was accidentally sent as an agent prompt. The resulting reply occurred after the recorded paint; it does not establish anything about full readiness.
Readiness and long-task attribution need explicit startup marks or a complete rendering trace. No source changes or deployment were performed during this recheck.
